purpose: Rebuild Japanese surface-combatant and submarine physical/readiness wallets from realized Branch events rather than historical loss-date inheritance; close narrative-only damage slots; identify remaining submarine uncertainty before Eastern Fleet simulation.
precedence_note: This working audit supersedes the old planning-only fleet-DD alive band 58-66 for Jan-1944 analysis if hull-by-hull reconciliation is accepted. It does not yet modify CURRENT_BRANCH_STATE until promoted.
method: Start from ships actually completed by the date.
Retain historical losses only where the causal theater/route/event still exists or a Branch-specific event recreates the loss.
Restore ships whose historical loss depended on absent Guadalcanal/Solomons/Rabaul/New-Guinea emergency chains unless a Branch substitute loss is realized.
Book Branch-specific Midway/New-Caledonia/Efate/Bengal/GALVANIC damage and losses explicitly.
Separate physical hull existence, machinery/crew readiness, mission allocation and theater-transfer availability.
Do not use the old July-1944 legacy DD roster as authority where it conflicts with current Branch-specific loss assignments.

fleet_destroyer_reconciliation.definition: modern fleet-type DD line: Fubuki/Akatsuki through Shimakaze; older Kamikaze/Mutsuki/Minekaze types are separate local-escort/transport pool
fleet_destroyer_reconciliation.allocation_note: Ready does not mean transferable. Carrier screens, Central Pacific reaction, South-Pacific bases, tanker/convoy protection and local fleets consume many hulls.
fleet_destroyer_reconciliation.comparison_to_old_planning_band: The Sep-1943 planning band 58-66 undercounted Jan-1944 physical hulls because it did not yet close absent-event Solomon losses hull-by-hull. Current settlements contain only three Branch-specific permanent modern-DD substitute losses (Yudachi, Natsugumo, Fubuki) plus retained non-Solomon losses listed above; do not force the new ledger back into the old band.
